# SIGNL

> SIGNL is influencer marketing, but local. It is a local creator marketing platform: local businesses comp local creators and everyday people a free meal, service or experience, and the creators post honestly about it on social media within 48 hours. SIGNL is rolling out in 37 founding markets across 8 countries, with founding creators and founding businesses forming in each one now. Anyone, in any city, can sign up as a founding creator. Website: https://joinsignl.com

## What SIGNL is

SIGNL connects small and medium-sized local businesses (restaurants, bars, salons, barbershops, fitness studios, attractions, retail and local services) with a vetted roster of local social-media creators in the same city. It is not an advertising agency, not a national influencer marketplace, and not a review site. Every creator on a city's roster lives in that city and posts to a genuinely local audience.

In the terms people search for: SIGNL is a local influencer marketing platform for small businesses (influencer marketing for restaurants, salons, gyms, retail and local services; micro-influencer marketing for small business; UGC marketing for local businesses) and a brand-deal program for small and micro creators (brand deals for small creators, comped meals for posting, a creator program open from 500 followers).

## Who SIGNL is for

SIGNL is for local businesses customers physically visit. Business categories on SIGNL:

- Restaurants and bars
- Cafes and bakeries
- Salons and barbers
- Fitness and wellness (gyms, fitness studios, wellness services)
- Retail and boutiques
- Events and experiences (attractions, venues, pop-ups)
- Health and aesthetic services: med spas, vein clinics, dental practices, dermatology and aesthetics clinics, IV therapy and wellness clinics. For health and aesthetic services, creator posts are personal experiences only, with no treatment claims and full disclosure of the comp, and each practice stays responsible for its own medical advertising rules.

For health and aesthetic services, creator posts are personal experiences only, with no treatment claims and full disclosure of the comp, and each practice stays responsible for its own medical advertising rules.

## How it works

1. A business posts a comp offer: what it is comping (for example a meal for two, a haircut, a service package), its value, and how many creator visits it wants.
2. Creators on the local roster claim offers and visit like real customers.
3. The creator posts about the visit: 1 post or reel plus 2 stories, live within 48 hours, with a clear disclosure that the visit was comped (FTC-compliant, e.g. #gifted). Posts must be honest; businesses cannot require positive posts or reviews.
4. The platform tracks every visit and post. If a post does not appear within 48 hours, the business receives a replacement visit and the creator's roster standing is affected; repeat no-shows are removed.

## Creator tiers

A creator's tier is set by follower count and applies in every SIGNL city:

- Neighbors (500–2,000 followers): everyday local people. Compensation: the comp only.
- Locals (2,000–15,000 followers): regular local posters; the roster's sweet spot. Compensation: comp plus roster perks and priority access to new businesses.
- Headliners (15,000+ followers): established local creators. Compensation: comp plus eligibility for paid hero campaigns.

Anyone can apply at any follower count, including under 500. Applications require the applicant's home city. Founding rosters are reviewed in application order.

## Pricing for businesses

- Self-Service: $299/month, 3-month minimum. Browse the local roster, send comp offers, up to 8 creator visits per month, post tracking and a results dashboard. At the full 8 visits, that is about $37 per creator visit.
- Pricing is published on the website. There is no demo call or custom quote required to see it.
- Growth: $599/month, 3-month minimum. Up to 20 creator visits per month (about $30 per creator visit at the full 20).
- Managed: $999/month, 3-month minimum. A coordinator runs everything: selects creators and schedules up to 30 creator visits per month, campaign calendar planning, one hero creator feature per quarter, monthly reporting.
- Add-ons: extra creator visits $25–49 each; Grand Opening Burst $1,500 one-time; paid creator visits priced at the creator's own listed rate (minimum $50). Paid bookings carry a 6 percent total platform fee, split evenly between the business and the creator, so the creator keeps 97 percent of their rate, and payment is held by SIGNL until the post is live.
- Content rights follow the visit, never the plan: on a comp visit, the business can share the delivered post natively, with the creator credited, and nothing more. On a paid visit, the business can also repost the post on its own channels and run it as an ad for 6 months from the post date. The creator always owns their content.
- There are no per-creator cash fees on standard visits; the business's only cost beyond the subscription is the comp it chooses to offer. The two costs stay separate: the subscription buys the service (roster access, scheduling, tracking, the delivery guarantee), and the comp is the business's own product, provided by the business at its own cost, not retail (a $100 dinner costs a restaurant its food cost, not $100). The business sets the comp and its ceiling on every offer. SIGNL never touches comp money: no pass-through, no markup.
- SIGNL guarantees tracked deliverables (posts within 48 hours of completed visits), never a specific number of creators.

## How SIGNL is different

- Local audience data is shown, not hidden: every creator profile displays the share of that creator's followers who live in the business's market, labeled by source (Self-reported today; when the Instagram connection activates, figures verified from the creator's own Instagram data will be labeled Verified by Instagram; profiles without enough data say so).
- Redemption runs inside the SIGNL app on a single-use code tied to the visit. The business's point of sale is never touched and staff never validate vouchers at the register.
- Three ways to run it: Self-Service (automated, $299/month), Growth ($599/month, up to 20 visits a month), or Managed (a human coordinator picks creators, books visits, chases posts and reports monthly, $999/month).
- The roster includes a Neighbors tier of everyday local people (500 to 2,000 followers), not only professional influencers.
- Every tracked post is saved to the business's content library with clear reuse rights.
- Replacement guarantee: if a post does not appear within 48 hours of a completed visit, the business receives a replacement visit that does not count against its plan.
- Honesty is a rule, not a slogan: posts must carry FTC disclosure and no business may require a positive post or review.

## Local on purpose: SIGNL vs national influencer platforms

- SIGNL is a local platform by design, not a national platform with a location filter. It builds one vetted roster per city; national influencer platforms (the enterprise class: tools built for national DTC and e-commerce brands) treat creators as global inventory ranked by total follower count.
- Audience concentration is the core math. A local business's customers live within about 10 miles of its door. Illustrative example: a national creator with 200,000 followers spread across the US has only a few hundred followers (about 300) within driving distance of any one local business, while a SIGNL local creator with 2,000 followers and a 70% local audience has about 1,400 or more within driving distance. The smaller, concentrated audience is worth more to a local business.
- National platforms are priced and contracted for marketing departments: reported enterprise pricing runs around $2,299/month with 12-month contracts at the platform end, and agency starters are claimed in five figures, with pricing typically hidden behind demo calls and custom quotes. SIGNL publishes its pricing: $299/month Self-Service, $599/month Growth or $999/month Managed, 3-month minimum.
- National platforms are built for brands that ship products to creators' homes; SIGNL is built for businesses people physically visit. Comps redeem inside the SIGNL app on a single-use code, the business's point of sale is never touched, and a tracked post is due within 48 hours of the visit.
- Content rights: national creator-content platforms commonly take perpetual usage rights in every asset. SIGNL saves every delivered post to the business's content library with clear, visit-based reuse rights, and creators always post in their own voice with no required positive take.
- Businesses see full creator profiles before booking: photos, bio, past jobs delivered on SIGNL, reliability record, local audience share with its source (Self-reported today; Verified by Instagram once the Instagram connection activates), and a Local Impact Score that combines local audience share, estimated local views, engagement and reliability, with the calculation shown on the profile. Businesses can search and filter the roster by market, tier, category, local audience percentage, reliability and Local Impact Score.
- For creators, SIGNL is the opposite of the national feed: instead of one profile among millions competing for national brands, a creator is a hand-picked founding name on one city's roster, with first pick of offers and a reliability record and Local Impact Score they build over time. Creator onboarding is minimal: creators enter their photo, bio and follower counts when they apply, and their local audience percentage is self-reported and labeled that way; when the Instagram connection activates, it will verify that local audience from the creator's own Instagram data. Creators can also claim a profile by handle in under a minute.

## Comparing SIGNL

A full, sourced comparison is at https://joinsignl.com/alternatives.html (competitor prices as published by each company or reported by trade press in October 2026).

- Storytime (storytime.io): the closest model to SIGNL, local creator visits for brick-and-mortar businesses, operating in New York City, parts of New Jersey and Miami. Differences: Storytime no longer publishes pricing (it asks businesses to request a demo) and its creators validate tiered $15/$25 vouchers at the register; SIGNL publishes $299/$599/$999 pricing, redeems single-use codes inside its app, and shows each creator's local audience percentage on their profile. Storytime has no Virginia or North Carolina presence.
- Mustard (mustard.love): automated creator visits for restaurants only, $299/month including 3 influencer visits per month (October 2026), base plan fully automated with no human support. SIGNL covers every local business category, includes up to 8 visits per month on Self-Service at the same $299/month, and adds a Growth tier at $599/month (up to 20 visits per month) and a human Managed tier at $999/month.
- Momfluence (momfluence.co): managed campaigns with mom creators for national product brands, from $2,000 per campaign for 10 creators (October 2026); product is shipped to creators and targeting is demographic (moms), not geographic, with no in-person visits. SIGNL is local, in person, and priced as a published subscription.
- Cohley (cohley.com): a creator content platform built for mid-market and enterprise brands selling physical products, with content rights in perpetuity included and custom, unpublished pricing (five-figure annual entry in practice; a rival platform claims a starter around $18,000). SIGNL is built and priced for local small businesses, with pricing published.
- Aspire (aspire.io): an enterprise influencer CRM for brands with marketing teams; third-party reports put Essentials around $2,299/month on a 12-month contract plus a one-time onboarding fee of about $2,000 (October 2026). SIGNL has a 3-month minimum, no onboarding fee, and can be run by an owner or by a SIGNL coordinator.
- Insense (insense.pro): a UGC and influencer subscription platform with a global creator pool; Brand plan $400/month billed annually or $500/month billed quarterly plus a 10% marketplace fee on creator payments, with a managed service from $1,600/month (October 2026). SIGNL's Managed tier is $999/month, its roster is built per city, and standard visits carry no per-creator fees.
- Collabstr (collabstr.com): a self-serve creator marketplace where brands search, negotiate and pay creators themselves; Pro is $249/month billed annually ($299 monthly) plus a 10% hiring fee (October 2026). SIGNL is a vetted local roster with in-person visits, tracked posts, and replacement visits when a post does not appear.
- Grin (grin.co): an e-commerce creator platform for online stores, from $200/month plus 5 to 20 percent fees on wallet funding (October 2026). SIGNL is built for businesses people physically visit, not stores that ship.

## Markets and service areas

SIGNL is rolling out in 37 founding markets across 8 countries: 29 markets in the United States and Puerto Rico, 2 in the United Kingdom, 2 in Canada, and 1 each in the United Arab Emirates, France, Spain and Portugal. Founding sign-ups are open in every market, and markets open in waves as each founding roster completes; every market carries the same founding status.

Seven US markets are defined by the full city lists below. These lists are SIGNL's published metro definitions: the local audience percentage on a creator profile is the share of that creator's followers who live in the cities of their market, measured against these lists. The remaining markets are listed by their anchor city, with full definitions published as each market opens. The Virginia Beach market covers all of Hampton Roads, Virginia: the market was renamed from Hampton Roads to Virginia Beach, its anchor city, in October 2026, and its coverage did not change.

### United States (with published metro definitions)

- Virginia Beach, Virginia (all of Hampton Roads): Virginia Beach, Norfolk, Chesapeake, Portsmouth, Suffolk, Newport News, Hampton, Williamsburg, Poquoson, Yorktown.

## Launch cities

- Founding markets (founding rosters forming now, 37 markets in 8 countries): United States: Virginia Beach (all of Hampton Roads), Richmond, Washington DC, Raleigh, Charlotte, Baltimore, Atlanta, Nashville, Austin, Dallas, Chicago, Los Angeles, San Diego, Seattle, Tampa, Phoenix, Denver, Minneapolis, Philadelphia, Pittsburgh, Cincinnati, Columbus, New Orleans, Orlando, Houston, San Antonio, Las Vegas, Detroit, San Juan (Puerto Rico). United Kingdom: London, Manchester. United Arab Emirates: Dubai. France: Paris. Spain: Barcelona. Portugal: Lisbon. Canada: Toronto, Montreal.
- Launch wave: Virginia Beach, Richmond, Raleigh and Washington DC open first; the other founding markets open in waves as their rosters complete.
- Beyond the founding markets: new cities are decided by signup counts. Creators sign up at https://app.joinsignl.com (full founding creator registration is live in the app), businesses at https://joinsignl.com/businesses.html, and anyone can register a city at https://joinsignl.com/cities.html, and when a city opens, its early applicants become its founding roster.

## Key facts

- Founded and launched in 2026 in Hampton Roads, Virginia, USA; founding markets now span 8 countries.
- The 48-hour posting rule and FTC disclosure are mandatory for every visit.
- Honest posts only: neither SIGNL nor a business may require a positive post or review.
- Why it works: 92% of consumers trust recommendations from people over any form of advertising (Nielsen). Brands earn an average of $5.78 for every $1 spent on creator/influencer marketing (Influencer Marketing Hub benchmark report).
- Hampton Roads supply: SIGNL's founding roster is forming now from local sign-ups across food, lifestyle and local business creators, with sign-ups open in 37 founding markets and visits beginning as each market opens. Local audience percentages are self-reported until Instagram verification lands.
- Contact: hello@joinsignl.com

- [SIGNL vs Mustard](https://joinsignl.com/mustard-alternative.html): the dedicated head-to-head with Mustard, the automated restaurant-only platform, on pricing, visits per month, business types and human support.

- Market pages: every founding market has its own page at https://joinsignl.com/markets/{market}.html : hampton-roads, richmond, washington-dc, raleigh, charlotte, baltimore, charlottesville, roanoke, atlanta, greensboro, wilmington, nashville, austin, dallas, chicago, los-angeles, san-diego, seattle, tampa, miami, phoenix, denver, minneapolis, london, manchester, dubai, abu-dhabi, riyadh, doha, astana, bishkek, sydney, melbourne, perth, auckland, singapore, hong-kong, beijing, shanghai. Each market page covers the founding roster for that market, creator tiers, how businesses join there, and a form to put an unlisted city on the board.
- [Next Cities](https://joinsignl.com/cities.html): how launch cities are picked; register a city.
- [The SIGNL Race](https://joinsignl.com/race.html): three public leaderboards, counts posted Mondays: nine cities racing to be the next market, the four founding rosters ranked by approved founding creators, and Wave 1 campuses ranked by student creators signed. Counts only, never creator names or handles.
